findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance's underlying EBS storage, snapshots and automated backups are stored in cleartext. Any compromise of the storage layer or a shared snapshot exposes all database contents.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public IP and public DNS name, making the MySQL endpoint reachable from the internet subject only to the attached security group. Combined with the exported db_endpoint output and an admin account, this creates a directly attackable data store.

The master password is supplied through var.password and the master username is the predictable default 'admin'; the password will be written in cleartext to the Terraform state file and is easily exposed through tfvars or CI variables. A predictable admin username on a publicly accessible instance also aids credential-guessing attacks.
iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so the database relies solely on a static master password rather than short-lived IAM-issued tokens for authentication.

No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (error, general, audit, slowquery) are configured, so authentication attempts and queries against an internet-facing database are not retained for detection or forensic review.
deletion_protection is not enabled and skip_final_snapshot = true, so an attacker or mistaken actor with RDS permissions can destroy the database irrecoverably with no final snapshot.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", giving any principal assuming this role (the EC2 instance via aws_iam_instance_profile.ec2profile) full control of all S3 buckets, EC2 resources and RDS databases in the account. This violates least privilege and creates a privilege-escalation/data-exfiltration path if the instance is compromised.

The egress rule allows all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database/app security group, permitting unrestricted outbound traffic that can be used for data exfiltration or command-and-control communication.

MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than to the specific application security group or subnet, allowing any host in the VPC (including any compromised or unrelated instance) to reach the database directly.

The database password (var.password) and username are interpolated directly into the EC2 user_data script, which is stored in plaintext in instance metadata and retrievable by anyone able to reach the IMDS endpoint (including via SSRF from the web app running on the instance) or with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute permissions.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's storage — which holds the dbinfo.inc file containing DB credentials — is created unencrypted at rest.

No metadata_options block is set, so the instance permits IMDSv1 (token-optional). Combined with a PHP application taking user input and an attached IAM instance profile, an SSRF in the app can retrieve role credentials from the metadata service.

The bootstrap script installs and starts httpd serving the employee-data application over plain HTTP only, with no TLS configuration, so submitted names and addresses and any session data traverse the network in cleartext.
